 Protecting Democracy Doesn't End on Election Day: Here's How We Build What Comes Next 
 November 9, 2026 Rabbi Lindsey Danziger 
 Image: 
 Elections matter. But protecting democracy does not begin or end on a Tuesday in November. It is built in the days between elections-through relationships, organizing, and the determination to show up for one another. In a moment when Jews are experiencing increased antisemitism and wondering if their voices are being heard, we are claiming our seat at the table in our nation's democracy.
 We saw that determination in Jackson, Mississippi. Earlier this year, Beth Israel Congregation was devastated by an antisemitic arson attack. Yet just days after the 2026 election, members of the local Jewish community joined a training to help voters correct problems with their ballots so their votes could count. In a moment when they had every reason to turn inward, they chose to serve their neighbors.
 That is what democratic resilience looks like.
 At the Religious Action Center of Reform Judaism (RAC), we believe Jewish communities are safer in a strong democracy. That's why, building on the Reform Movement's Every Voice, Every Vote campaign, we're launching We All Belong: A Jewish Campaign for Democracy, Safety, and Freedom in 2027. Join us by completing the Covenant to Protect Democracy today!
 We're moving from election protection to year-round democracy building.
 What if, by 2028, our congregations have spent two years building deep relationships with neighbors and community partners across differences? What if our members have the skills to organize, the ability to have difficult conversations, and the commitment to mobilize others? What if our elected officials already know who we are because we've built relationships with them long before a crisis?
 Imagine shifting from reacting to threats as they emerge to proactively shaping the future we want to see . Instead of scrambling to respond in moments of urgency, we could draw on strong networks, trusted relationships, and shared strategies to act early, advocate effectively, and build lasting change.
 That's the power of year-round democratic organizing. And that's the future we're building through We All Belong.
 Four Ways to Build Democracy in Your Community
 Start or strengthen a Democracy Builder Team. 
Bring people together in your congregation or community to turn shared values into sustained local action. If you helped lead a Protect Our Vote Team, consider transforming it into a Democracy Builder Team to strengthen civic engagement in your community. W, we will provide trainings and resources for every step.
 Build relationships with elected officials. 
Join our efforts to organize or participate in in-district meetings with local, state, and federal representatives. We will train you and provide support and resources. When legislators know our communities and priorities before a crisis arises, we can advocate more effectively for democracy, justice, and safety.
 Get trained to defend rights and freedoms. 
Learn to recognize and respond to threats to our democracy and our communities. Trainings can help us develop practical skills, organize effectively, and meet difficult moments with confidence.
 Strengthen relationships across differences. 
Reach beyond your congregation. Learn how to build genuine partnerships with neighbors and organizations whose backgrounds or experiences differ from yours, so we are ready to stand together when it matters.
 Your connections matter, too . If you know an elected official or a member of their staff, share that relationship through our Covenant to Protect Democracy form. Those connections will help RAC staff coordinate future meetings and build long-term influence.
 Take Action Today
 Complete the Covenant to Protect Democracy to tell us which opportunities interest you. You don't need to commit to everything; every person has a role to play.
 You can also sign the Reform Jewish Movement's open letter to the incoming 120th Congress , join our January 27, 2027, Democracy Builder Orientation , and reserve your place at Consultation on Conscience , December 5-7, 2027 , in Washington, DC.
 Our goal is not simply to prepare for the next election; it's to build communities that are more connected, more powerful, and more resilient because of what we do together between elections.
 We all belong. And we all have a part to play.

 About the Author
 Rabbi Lindsey Danziger
 Rabbi Lindsey Danziger (she/her) is the Director of Campaigns at the Religious Action Center of Reform Judaism . She works with Reform Jewish congregations and communities across the United States and Canada to build the leadership, relationships, and collective power needed to create a more just and compassionate society in the United States and Israel.
